

-- openstack service token
-- generated by aI

-- OPENSTACK SERVICE TOKENS: CONFIGURATION & SETUP GUIDE

-- KEYSTONE SETUP
Create a dedicated 'service' role and assign it to the nova service account:

# Create the service role (if it doesn't already exist)
openstack role create service

# Grant the service role to the nova user on the service project
openstack role add \
  --project service \
  --user nova \
  --user-domain Default \
  --project-domain Default \
  service


-- (/etc/nova/nova.conf)
Edit /etc/nova/nova.conf across control plane nodes also set this to compute nodes:

[service_user]
send_service_user_token = true
auth_type = password
auth_url = http://controller:5000/v3
project_domain_name = Default
user_domain_name = Default
project_name = service
username = nova
password = NOVA_SERVICE_PASSWORD

[keystone_authtoken]
service_token_roles = service
service_token_roles_required = true


-- RECEIVING SERVICES CONFIGURATION
In /etc/cinder/cinder.conf,
 /etc/neutron/neutron.conf,
 /etc/glance/glance-api.conf:

[keystone_authtoken]
service_token_roles = service
service_token_roles_required = true


-- RESTART SERVICES
sudo systemctl restart \
 openstack-nova-api.service \
 openstack-nova-conductor.service \
 openstack-nova-scheduler.service


-- VERIFICATION
-- Set debug = true in /etc/nova/nova.conf and inspect /var/log/nova/nova-api.log.

-- Verify outgoing API calls contain both headers:
  - X-Auth-Token: The end user's token.
  - X-Service-Token: Nova's service token.
